messages:
dave: alert from west-us-prod: sudden allocation failures on a subset of inferencers, one node OOM'd. posting raw trace id: 5a9c. kernel selector logged a fallthrough to cpu_fallback_kernel; workspace allocator reported fragmentation during KV+workspace reservation. starting thread to coordinate mitigation steps.
alice: saw the same in perf-monitor: large concurrent long-context requests + a sustained spike in batch coalescing. dynamic_batcher pushed a few 32-sized batches for seq~6k which killed contiguous allocation.
ben: looks like sticky sessions kept KV frames alive and small allocations fragmented the heap. suggest two-pronged: short-term allocator flag to prioritize contiguous free coalescing + enable buffer_reuse; medium-term: per-session KV caps and proactive eviction.
carol: oncall runbook enacted: isolate node, drain, mark unhealthy. Circuits show node_pool_westus triggered workspace_circuit at 1930005140. infra-bot: [auto] Circuit opened for pool-westus at 1930005140 due to workspace_exhaustion (metric: workspace_fail_rate>4%).
eve: Quick mitigation: 1) set allocator.coalesce_free=true 2) allocator.reuse_buffers=soft 3) runtime.dynamic_batch_max=16 for interactive routes 4) route large embeddings (>8192 tokens) to compact-embed model or stream-truncate.
dave: hotfix prepared: reuse_buffers reduces total contiguous requirement by consolidating per-request temp buffers. still need to cap per-session KV bytes to avoid runaway sessions. propose kv.max_session_mb=48 and kv.idle_eviction_secs=180.
alice: microbench on staging: with reuse_buffers=soft and coalesce_free enabled, peak reserved went down ~22% for mixed chat+embed workload (seq=4096, mix ratio 70/30). tail p99 latency increased ~15ms on fused kernels due to extra memcpy. acceptable trade during emergency.
ben: also implement a scheduling policy change: when kernel selection predicts contiguous_failure, prefer smaller-kernel variant (fused->split attention or quantized kernel) ahead of time instead of waiting for allocation fail. we can add a cheap estimator: contiguous_needed = base_workspace(seq_len,batch) + kv_active_bytes. if > free_contiguous_threshold then preempt to compact kernel.
carol: immediate ops actions: apply allocator flags to canary group (10% west-us), reduce dynamic_batch_max on west-us pool to 16; add token-based throttles for partner API keys (throttle if token_rate>4000/min). also set circuit-breaker sensitivity: open if kernel_fallback_rate>3% over 2min.
dave: I'll push canary config PR: runtime#4871. Canary will run for 30 minutes; metrics to watch: p95 latency, kernel_fallback_rate, contiguous_free_bytes, kv_growth_rate.
infra-bot: [auto] Canary deploy started: canary-westus-A (10% nodes). Monitoring endpoints: /vitals/canary-westus-a.
eve: fallback ladder in runbook: 1) reuse_buffers + coalesce_free; 2) preemptive kernel choice to compact kernels; 3) aggressive KV eviction for sessions idle>180s; 4) force truncate/drop >12000 tokens requests (return 413) if pattern repeats.
alice: adding a minor tweak: allocator.workspace_target_ratio=0.7 to lower per-kernel workspace ambitions and reduce contiguous reservation pressure.
ben: partner throttle applied to offending api-key. partner reported a batch job misconfigured to send 50 simultaneous long-context requests; they acknowledged and will stagger.
ave: (typo) sorry, meant eve.
carol: Monitoring update at 1930006160: canary stable for 10m, kernel_fallback_rate dropped from 6.1%->1.1%, contiguous_free_bytes rising. Rolling to 50% per plan if stable for 20m.
dave: note for post-incident: we should add a simulator that runs the contiguous allocator on sampled workloads to surface fragmentation risk before deploys. also add an eval that stresses KV growth from sticky sessions.
alice: profiling artifact: /internal/profiles/1930005123/alloc-frag-5a9c.html attached to PR. timeline shows first allocation fail at 1930005138 and last at 1930005152.
ben: follow-up ops doc snippets: if OOM repeats after these changes -> 1) immediately throttle by token_count and per-key concurrency 2) escalate to forced_kv_eviction on allocation failure path 3) increase soft_reserve_percent by +12% for high-risk kernels 4) if still unstable, temporarily demote route to hosted-compact models.
carol: rolling update: 1930006680 canary at 50% shows stable metrics, rolling to 100% now. will keep circuit sensitivity higher for 2hrs. Closing incident if no flares by 1930007280. Please keep logs and traces for the postmortem.
dave: final note: long-term work items: predictive kernel selection based on contiguous estimator, defragmenting allocator sweep, KV per-session budget enforcement in control plane, and a partner-rate-limit policy. I'll add to backlog and tag eng-runtime.
carol: thanks team. short updates only here while we watch. ping @dave for any new large trace ids.
